em.why: no pinned source states CR0.EM of the declared machine (ks386.inc CR0_EM is a bit constant only; Wine runs on the host CPU); user mode observes CR0 only through smsw, which is itself undecided; blocker: a reach certificate that no site depends on it, or an owner decision to derive it from the CPUID record

mp.why: no pinned source states CR0.MP (ks386.inc CR0_MP is a bit constant only); user mode sees it only through smsw (undecided)

ts.why: no pinned source; user mode sees TS only through smsw (undecided); Windows handles #NM transparently (lazy FPU switch), and the lazy-switch behaviour is not a pinned source

pce.why: rdpmc at CPL 3 needs CR4.PCE = 1; the SDM only defines the bit, the declared CPU's cpuid does not state it, the WDK 7.1 constants name no PCE bit and Wine 9.0 has no rdpmc case

tsd.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr intercepts only the 0F opcodes ['0x20', '0x21', '0x22', '0x23'], so rdtsc (0F 31) runs in user mode; consistent with the owner's decision that rdtsc reads the platform timer

umip.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 2.5 CR4.UMIP: the bit is reserved (setting it is #GP) unless CPUID.(EAX=07H,ECX=0):ECX[2] is enumerated; the declared CPU's max basic leaf is 4 (ports/fnv-nx/verify/cpuid_model.json max_basic @ a3217cd2c604), below 7, so there is no leaf 7 and CR4.UMIP is 0

osfxsr.source: derived: CR4.OSFXSR = 1 iff the declared PF_XMMI_INSTRUCTIONS_AVAILABLE (row processor_features[6]) is TRUE, because MSDN IsProcessorFeaturePresent gives that value the meaning 'the SSE instruction set is available' to the calling process and Intel SDM Vol 3A 2.5 / 13.1 raises #UD for SSE instructions when CR4.OSFXSR = 0; ks386.inc CR4_FXSR = 0x200 names the bit

osxmmexcpt.why: no pinned source states CR4.OSXMMEXCPT (ks386.inc CR4_XMMEXCPT = 0x400 is a bit constant only); with the initial MXCSR 0x1F80 every SIMD exception is masked, so #XM is not raised until a site unmasks it; blocker: a certificate that every ldmxcsr / fxrstor site keeps the exceptions masked (CLAUDE.md fact, not yet certified)

initial.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: the initial thread context, context.EFlags

iopl.source: bits 12-13 of the initial EFLAGS (Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6)

iopl_user_modifiable.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): EFLAGS_USER_SANITIZE = 0x3F4DD7, the EFLAGS bits user code can set; bits 12-13 are not in it

idtr_limit.why: the number of gates of the OS's IDT is not stated by a pinned source (the SDM allows 256 entries at most)

41.why: MSDN __fastfail intrinsic: fast fail is supported from Windows 8 (build 9200); Windows 7 SP1 is build 7601, so int 0x29 is not a fast-fail gate there. What the instruction does on build 7601 is not stated by MSDN: undecided

other_vectors.why: no pinned source says whether Windows 7 has a ring-3 gate at any other vector; Wine 9.0 handles only these

int_ring3.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: handle_interrupt cases ['0x2d']; segv_handler / trap_handler map ['TRAP_x86_BPTFLT', 'TRAP_x86_OFLOW'] to #OF / #BP

ss.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3; ss needs a writable data segment, not the null selector

undecided.why: the ring-3 code descriptor's readable bit is not stated in a pinned source, so whether es/ds/fs/gs may load it is undecided

precedence: (1) documented Win32 for Windows 7 SP1 build 7601: MSDN and WDK 7.1
(2) Wine 9.0, only where it contradicts neither (1) nor the declared OS
(3) nothing else (ReactOS is not a source)

others.source: MSDN IsProcessorFeaturePresent, return value: zero when the feature is not supported; the WDK 7.1 winnt.h defines indices 0..17 only. Wine 9.0 also sets higher indices of newer Windows (e.g. PF_FASTFAIL_AVAILABLE, Windows 8+), which contradicts the declared build 7601 (precedence 1: documentation).

tss_io_bitmap.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr returns EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION for every in/out/ins/outs form with no per-port test (the instruction set is L3b's sdm_priv_rows.tsv, iopl class, not restated here), i.e. a Win32 user process has no permitted port; the documentation names the TSS I/O map (WDK 7.1 ks386.inc TssIoMapBase = 0x66, PrIopmOffset = 0x6E) and the exception (MSDN EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION: an instruction not allowed in the current machine mode) but states no permitted port for a user process, so it does not contradict Wine (precedence 2); with IOPL 0 (row eflags) every such instruction at CPL 3 is #GP(0), delivered as that exception
